headline: ALL per-member delivery values are in the publisher SOURCE DATA workbook 41467_2026_69077_MOESM6_ESM.xlsx (TIER 1), at per-replicate resolution. ALL structures are in the Supplementary Information PDF as full IUPAC names plus HRMS formulas (TIER 4 text, pp 18-50). NOTHING in this curation needs pixels. Zero panels are read geometrically.

library_size.recorded_in_task: not recorded -- establishing it was the first job

established.amide/ester-coupled CBB series: CBB1-CBB22 (22 compounds). CBB22 is commercial Coomassie Brilliant Blue G-250 itself; CBB21 is the bis(K1-diamine) sulfonamide core made from it; CBB1-20 are CBB21 bis-acylated (or CBB G-250 bis-esterified, for CBB15/16).
established.oxidation product: CBBox11 (1) -- two hydroxylation isomers, SI Fig 2
established.click/triazole CBBZ series: CBBZ0 (the propargyl-ether dye scaffold) + CBBZ1-CBBZ10 (10 conjugates) = 11
established.screened with a value: CBB1-22 (Fig 2c, Fig 4c), CBBox11 + CBB14 + CBBZ1-Z10 (Fig 2d), CBB11 + CBBZ1-Z7 (Fig 4d)
established.how_established: SI pp 18-50 compound headings ('(Compound CBBn)'), each with its own HRMS, cross-read against the Source Data column headers of Fig 2c/2d/4c/4d and against the main text sentence 'among CBB1-22 and CBBZ1-Z7'.
established.NO combinatorial enumeration: Despite the title's 'combinatorial synthetic strategy', this is NOT a block x block enumeration with a multiplicative size. Every member is an individually named, individually purified, individually HRMS-characterised compound. There is no Markush grid and no stated library size to reconcile against: the honest statement is 34 named compounds, not a product of block counts. 01_blocks.csv therefore records the ACTUAL two-position decomposition (dye scaffold x tail) that the syntheses use, and 03_enumerated.csv has one row per named compound.

cargo.WARNING: This is PROTEIN / RNP delivery, not mRNA transfection. A different cargo is a different experiment.

cargo_2.name: ABE8e ribonucleoprotein (adenine base editor ABE8e + sgRNA)

tiers.layout: row 1 = column headers 1..22 then LF, C, NE; rows 2-5 = 4 replicates
tiers.why_not_lower_tier: n/a -- this IS tier 1; no figure was read.

tiers.layout: row 6 = headers ox11, 14, Z1..Z10, LF, C, NE; rows 7-8 = replicates
tiers.method: fluorescence microscopy only (NOT flow) -- the legend says so explicitly, and the CBB14 value differs from Fig 2c's, so the two panels are different assays and must not be pooled

tiers.cargo: Cre (upper block) and ABE8e RNP (lower block)
tiers.why: a dose-ratio titration on 9 selected compounds, not a library screen; its 8:1 row is the condition Fig 2c/4c already report. Kept as the independent cross-check that 8:1 is the emitted ratio.

in vivo (subretinal, mouse eye) and liposome-formulation panels. The varying unit is the FORMULATION (Lipo1-8) or the mouse, not the library member: only CBB6/11/14/ox11 appear, at n<=6 eyes, and the readouts are ERG b-wave amplitude (uV), 11-cis-retinal (pmol), and % DNA/cDNA editing. No library-wide in vivo screen exists in this paper, so there is no in vivo row set to emit.
viability (% DAPI-negative), not delivery. Recorded here so a later reader does not mistake it for a second screen.

tiers.what: 'Synthesis of CBB intermediates and lipidoids'. Every compound carries its full IUPAC name, 1H/13C NMR, and 'HRMS calculated for <formula>, <m/z>; found <m/z> (error <x> ppm)'. The IUPAC name IS the connectivity; the HRMS formula is an independent arm-count check.
tiers.why_not_tier_1_2_3: tier 1: the Source Data workbook carries values and LC-MS traces, no structures. tier 2: there is no SI structure table -- SI Figs 1 and 3 are schematics, not tables. tier 3: no author repository exists (find_repo.py, 0 repo_hits across the DOI, PMID, title and author sweeps). So the SI text is the highest tier that holds structures, and it is a TEXT layer, not pixels.

tiers.why_listed: Rendered and LOOKED AT only to confirm, by eye, the two things a name cannot settle on its own: that acylation is on the terminal primary amine (not the internal tertiary one) and that the CBBZ triazole is 1,4. No number and no SMILES is taken from a pixel.

github_check.command: python3 -I find_repo.py --doi 10.1038/s41467-026-69077-w --pmid 41654520 --title 'combinatorial genome editing delivery' --author Palczewski
github_check.note: 18 candidates all filtered out as unrelated. The paper's Code availability / Data availability makes no repository claim. Tier 3 is genuinely unavailable.

risk_register: Fig 2d and Fig 4d are MICROSCOPY while Fig 2c and Fig 4c are FLOW on the same reporter line. CBB14 reads 58.2% (2c, flow) vs 31.95% (2d, microscopy) and CBB11 reads 28.6% (4c, flow) vs 53.3% (4d, microscopy). Same compound, same cargo, same cell line, different instrument -> ~2x either way. These are four separate assay blocks, not one screen.
Fig 2c / 4c share the SAME 22 compounds, so the two cargoes give a within-lab, same-chemistry, cargo-swap concordance point (directly relevant to CLAUDE.md section 8's molea.csv rung).

CBB22 is the unmodified commercial dye and CBB21 is the un-acylated core; both are library members with values, and both are legitimate 'no tail' points rather than controls. LF (Lipofectamine 3000), C (cargo only), A (ABE8e only) and NE (no enzyme) ARE controls and are NOT emitted as library members.
